#### SE-S-070 – Production Schedule

**Business Intent:** Maintain the enterprise’s continuously current understanding of how production will be sequenced and timed across constrained resources to realize the Supply Plan, respecting finite capacity, changeovers, material availability, and operational constraints.

**Enterprise Meaning:** *(combined from original Purpose and Definition)*  
The Production Schedule is the aggregate root that maintains the current production schedule for one constrained resource over one planning period. It records the ordered sequence of production activities with their timing, changeovers, resource assignments, and synchronization dependencies. It assesses schedule feasibility against material, capacity, tool, labor, and maintenance constraints. It captures the decision rationale and evidence for every sequencing choice. It tracks schedule stability relative to previous versions.

**Identity:** Resource (Physical Resource SE-C-007) + Planning Period + Schedule Type (where multiple independent schedules exist for the same resource-period; default: Primary). The model supports Primary, Recovery, Frozen, and Scenario schedules without architectural change.

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Schedule Production (CA-S-007) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The current, executable production schedule for a resource and period. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Sequence production, assess feasibility, confidence, and stability. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per resource, per planning period. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Published Production Schedule (SE-S-071), Production Execution (external), Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |
| **Supersedes** | The previous Active schedule for the same resource-period. |
| **Superseded By** | A materially revised schedule for the same resource-period. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | At any moment, exactly one Active Production Schedule exists for each resource-period combination. The schedule respects all hard constraints. Sequencing decisions are documented with rationale and evidence. Versions are immutable once superseded or archived. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall treat the schedule as the authoritative production sequence. It does not constitute job dispatch. |
| **Known Limitations** | Does not include real-time execution status or unplanned downtime events. |
| **Version Expectations** | Active → Superseded (when materially revised) → Archived. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Updated when Supply Plan, capacity assessments, or material availability changes materially. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Published Production Schedule, Production Execution, Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**

| State | Description | Transition Trigger |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| Active | Current, authoritative schedule for the resource-period. | AB-S-060 |
| Superseded | Replaced by a materially revised schedule. | Material revision |
| Archived | Planning period has passed. | Archive operation |

- **Terminal States:** Archived.
- **History Preservation:** All versions retained permanently.

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Type | Description |
|----------|-------------|------|-------------|
| Identity | Resource, Planning Period, Version | Mandatory | Unique version identity within the resource-period. |
| Sequence | Ordered list of Production Activities (activity identifier, product, quantity, start time, end time, duration, preceding activity, succeeding activity) | Derived | The ordered production sequence. Order is enterprise knowledge: A→B→C differs from C→A→B. |
| Campaigns | Campaign grouping of consecutive production activities sharing common setup, material, or process characteristics; campaign boundaries defined by changeover triggers | Derived | Campaign scheduling minimises changeovers and contamination risk. |
| Changeovers | Per-transition changeover type, setup time, cleaning time, tooling change time | Derived | Changeover details between consecutive activities. |
| Resource Assignment | Specific resource assigned, equivalent resources considered, alternate resource evaluated, overtime applied | Derived | Which resource executes each activity, and what flexibility was exercised. |
| Synchronization | Cross-resource dependencies, labor synchronization points, tool synchronization points, material synchronization points | Derived | Multi-resource coordination requirements. Material availability is time-sensitive. |
| Schedule Feasibility | Overall Feasibility (Feasible, Conditionally Feasible, Infeasible), per-constraint feasibility: Material Availability, Capacity Availability, Tool Availability, Labor Availability, Maintenance Conflict, Calendar Conflict, Frozen Horizon Compliance | Derived | Whether the schedule is actually executable. Each constraint independently assessed. |
| Schedule Confidence | Overall Confidence Score, Material Certainty, Resource Reliability, Changeover Accuracy, Demand Stability | Derived | Multi-dimensional confidence in the schedule’s executability. |
| Schedule Criticality | Per-activity criticality classification: Critical Path Activity, Bottleneck Activity, Flexible Activity | Derived | Enterprise understanding of which schedule elements are most important. |
| Decision Evidence | Source Supply Plan ID, Inventory Position Assessments used, Capacity Position Assessments used, Material Availability Confirmations, Scheduling Policy version | Mandatory | Structured references to the evidence that informed scheduling decisions. |
| Decision Rationale | Why this sequence, why this resource, why overtime, why a setup was preferred, why an activity was deferred, why the sequence changed | Optional | Business-language explanation of key scheduling choices. |
| Schedule Stability | Stability Score, Change Count since previous version, Change Magnitude | Derived | How much the schedule has changed relative to the previous version. |
| Traceability | Created Timestamp, Last Updated Timestamp, Source Supply Plan Version | Mandatory | Evidence lineage. |

**Relationships**

| Relationship | Target Object | Cardinality | Description |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| schedules work on | Physical Resource (SE-C-007) | Many-to-One | The resource scheduled. |
| realises plan from | Supply Plan (SE-S-020) | Many-to-One | The supply plan driving the schedule. |
| uses capacity assessment | Capacity Position Assessment (SE-S-040) | Many-to-One | Constraint data. |
| uses inventory assessment | Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030) | Many-to-One | Material availability. |
| uses supplier commitments | Supplier Commitment (SE-S-050) | Many-to-One | Inbound material confirmation. |

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Type | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|

| Supply Domain Dependency | Supply Plan (SE-S-020), Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030), Capacity Position Assessment (SE-S-040), Supplier Commitment (SE-S-050). |

#### AB-S-060 — Create Production Schedule


**Purpose:** For a given resource and planning period, sequence production activities, assess feasibility, compute confidence and stability, and record the scheduling rationale and evidence.

**Business Intent:** Transform the Supply Plan’s planned production quantities into an executable, sequenced, time-phased production schedule.

**Trigger:** Supply Plan published, Capacity Position Assessment changed, or scheduled re-evaluation.

**Preconditions:** Supply Plan (SE-S-020) has planned production quantities; Capacity Position Assessment (SE-S-040) is current; Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030) confirms material availability; Supplier Commitment (SE-S-050) confirms inbound materials.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- Physical Resource (SE-C-007) is active.
- Calendar (SE-C-033) is current.
- Supply Plan (SE-S-020) has planned production quantities for this resource and period.
- Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030) is current for required materials.
- Capacity Position Assessment (SE-S-040) is current for this resource.
- Supplier Commitments (SE-S-050) confirm inbound material availability.

**Business Behaviour:** Invoke BA-S-040 to construct the schedule. Execute DE-S-061 to determine the production sequence and DE-S-062 to assess schedule feasibility. Record the decision rationale, evidence, confidence, and stability.

**State Transitions:**
- Required Input State: None (creation) or Active (revision).
- Produced Output State: Active (previous version → Superseded if revised).

**Business Transaction:** Protects Production Schedule aggregate. Atomic creation of sequence and metadata.

**Decisions Invoked:** DE-S-061 (Determine Production Sequence), DE-S-062 (Assess Schedule Feasibility).

**Rules Enforced:** BR-S-120 (Sequencing rules), BR-S-121 (Changeover minimization), BR-S-122 (Due date adherence), BR-S-123 (Priority adherence), BR-S-124 (Material availability), BR-S-125 (Capacity availability), BR-S-126 (Tool availability), BR-S-127 (Labor availability), BR-S-128 (Maintenance and calendar conflicts).

**Policies Referenced:** PO-S-080 (Scheduling Policy).

**Algorithms Invoked:** BA-S-040 (Construct Production Schedule).

**Events Published:** EV-S-060 (Production Schedule Created).

**Notifications Produced:** BN-S-060 (if created or materially revised).

**Idempotency:** Re-evaluation with same inputs produces same schedule.

**Concurrency:** Schedules for different resource-periods processed independently.

**Exceptional Conditions:** If material availability is missing, the schedule is constructed with flags. If capacity is insufficient and no overtime permitted, the schedule is Conditionally Feasible.

**Postconditions:** A current Production Schedule exists. BN-S-060 published if changed.

**Traceability:** Owned by SE-S-070. Invoked by FS-S-070.

#### SE-S-080 – Distribution Recommendation

**Business Intent**
Maintain the enterprise’s continuously current network positioning decision for each distribution requirement—recording where supply should be sourced, which lanes used, when movement should occur, why, with what confidence, and under what allocation strategy when supply is constrained.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The Distribution Recommendation is the aggregate root that maintains the current distribution recommendation for one distribution requirement. It captures the requirement itself, the movement decision (source locations, lanes, quantities, timing), the distribution strategy (preferred and alternative), allocation strategy when supply is constrained (policy used and allocation outcome), feasibility, confidence, stability, and decision evidence. The model supports any network topology—Supplier→Plant→DC→Regional DC→Warehouse→Customer—without assuming storage at intermediate nodes (cross-dock flows are natively supported).

**Identity**
Distribution Requirement Reference + Version. Anchored to the underlying requirement (e.g., Supply Plan transfer requirement, Inventory rebalancing trigger). Item, Source, Destination, Required Date are business attributes.

**Semantic Ownership**

| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| Primary Consumers    | Distribution Plan (SE-S-081), Distribution Execution (external), Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality |

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The continuously maintained, governed network positioning decision for a distribution requirement. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Determine the optimal movement plan, assess feasibility, and record rationale, evidence, and allocation outcomes. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per distribution requirement. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Distribution Plan (SE-S-081 — published baseline), Distribution Execution (external — shipment creation), Explain Supply Decisions (movement rationale), Evaluate Supply Quality (plan adherence). |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |
| **Supersedes** | The previous Active version for the same requirement. |
| **Superseded By** | A newer Active version for the same requirement. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | At any moment, exactly one Active Distribution Recommendation exists for each distribution requirement. The recommendation must be derived from the current Supply Plan, Inventory Position Assessments, and network data. When supply is constrained, both the allocation policy used and the allocation outcome must be recorded. Decision evidence must reference the specific artifacts used. Versions are immutable once superseded or archived. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall use the recommendation as the authoritative movement decision. The recommendation does not create shipments; execution systems consume the published Distribution Plan. |
| **Known Limitations** | The recommendation is a planning decision, not an execution order. Inventory availability and lane capacity may change after the recommendation is made. |
| **Version Expectations** | Continuously maintained; superseded versions retained permanently. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Updated upon Supply Plan changes, Inventory Position Assessment changes, or material revisions to the distribution situation. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Distribution Plan, Distribution Execution, Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**

| State | Description | Transition Trigger |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| Active | Current, authoritative recommendation. | AB-S-070 (Create or Revise) |
| Superseded | Replaced by a materially revised recommendation. | A newer version becomes Active |
| Archived | Requirement is no longer active. | Archive operation |

- **Terminal States:** Archived (final state retained permanently).
- **History Preservation:** All versions retained permanently. Superseded and Archived versions are immutable.

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Type | Description |
|----------|-------------|------|-------------|
| Identity | Distribution Requirement Reference, Version | Mandatory | Anchored to the requirement. |
| Requirement | Item (SE-C-001), Required Quantity, Source (where supply is needed), Destination (where demand exists), Required Date | Mandatory | The network positioning need. |
| Movement Decision | Source Location(s) (SE-C-002), Quantity per source, Lane(s) used (SE-C-008), Departure Timing (considering transit lead time), Destination Receiving Window | Derived | The specific movement plan. Inventory is projected to be available at the source at departure time; a unit arriving at the source on Friday cannot be moved on Wednesday. |
| Distribution Strategy | Preferred Distribution Strategy (primary source, primary lane, primary timing), Alternative Distribution Strategy (alternate source, alternate lane, alternate timing) | Mandatory | Enterprise understanding of the optimal and fallback positioning strategies. Strategies may differ in source location, intermediate nodes, lanes, or replenishment patterns—not merely alternative routes. |
| Allocation Strategy | Allocation Policy Used (Fair Share, Strategic Customer Priority, Region Priority, Service Level Priority, Promotion Support), Allocation Outcome (who received less, who received more, who was deferred, and by what quantity) | Derived | Applied only when available deployable inventory is insufficient to satisfy all requirements. Captures both the rule applied and the business consequence. |
| Deployment Priority | Service Protection, Promotion Support, New Product Launch, Seasonal Positioning, Inventory Balancing | Optional | The business purpose driving the deployment decision. |
| Distribution Feasibility | Source Inventory Availability, Lane Capacity Availability, Transit Time Feasibility, Destination Receiving Capacity (dock capacity, storage availability, handling capability), Time Window Achievability | Derived | Whether the movement is actually executable. Each constraint independently assessed. |
| Confidence | Inventory Certainty, Lane Reliability, Transit Time Accuracy, Receiving Capacity Confidence, Demand Volatility, Disruption Exposure | Derived | Multi-dimensional confidence in the recommendation. |
| Decision Rationale | Why this source, why this lane, why this timing, why inventory was intentionally retained (e.g., "Supply retained at DC-West because downstream demand uncertainty exceeded transfer benefit"), why this allocation outcome | Optional | Business-language explanation of the movement decision and any deliberate non-movement. |
| Decision Evidence | Source Supply Plan ID, Inventory Position Assessments used, Lane capacity data, Allocation Policy version | Mandatory | Structured references to evidence. |
| Stability | Change Count, Change Magnitude relative to previous version | Derived | How much the recommendation has changed. |
| Traceability | Created Timestamp, Last Updated Timestamp | Mandatory | Evidence lineage. |

| to destination location | Location (SE-C-002) | Many-to-One | Destination location. |
| uses lane | Transportation Lane (SE-C-008) | Many-to-Many | Lanes used. |
| references evidence from | Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030) | Many-to-Many | Inventory assessments. |
| references evidence from | Procurement Plan (SE-S-061) | Many-to-Many | Inbound procurement timing. |
| references evidence from | Production Schedule (SE-S-071) | Many-to-Many | Production completion timing. |
| references evidence from | Supplier Commitment (SE-S-050) | Many-to-Many | Inbound material availability. |

|-----------------|-------------|

| Supply Domain Dependency | Supply Plan (SE-S-020), Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030), Procurement Plan (SE-S-061), Production Schedule (SE-S-071), Supplier Commitment (SE-S-050). |

- At any moment, exactly one Active Distribution Recommendation exists for each distribution requirement.

- Decision evidence must reference the specific artifacts used.
- Versions are immutable once superseded or archived.

#### AB-S-070 — Create Distribution Recommendation


**Purpose:** For a given distribution requirement, evaluate source locations, lanes, constraints, and costs to produce a movement decision with full rationale, evidence, confidence, strategy, and allocation outcome.

**Business Intent:** Provide the authoritative, governed network positioning decision for each distribution requirement.

**Trigger:** Supply Plan published (new or changed transfer requirements), Inventory Position Assessment changed (shortages or excesses triggering rebalancing), or scheduled re-evaluation.

**Preconditions:** Supply Plan (SE-S-020) identifies the distribution requirement. Inventory Position Assessments (SE-S-030) are current. Network and lane master data are available.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- Item (SE-C-001) and Location (SE-C-002) exist and are active.
- Transportation Lane (SE-C-008) definitions are complete.
- Supply Plan (SE-S-020) has a Published version.
- Inventory Position Assessments (SE-S-030) are current for the source and destination locations.
- Governing policies (PO-S-090) are current.

**Business Behaviour:** Evaluate source locations against inventory availability, lane capacity, transit time, and receiving constraints.  Determine the optimal movement plan, distribution strategy, and deployment priority.  If supply is constrained, apply the allocation strategy and record the allocation outcome.  Assess distribution feasibility and multi-dimensional confidence.  Record decision rationale and evidence.  If materially different from the previous Active version, supersede the previous version.

**State Transitions:**
- **Required Input State:** None (creation) or Active (revision).
- **Produced Output State:** Active (previous version → Superseded if revised).

**Business Transaction:** Protects Distribution Recommendation aggregate.  Atomic creation or revision.

**Decisions Invoked:** DE-S-080 (Determine Distribution Sourcing).

**Rules Enforced:** BR-S-140–145.

**Policies Referenced:** PO-S-090 (Distribution Policy).

**Algorithms Invoked:** BA-S-050 (Construct Distribution Recommendation).

**Events Published:** EV-S-070 (Distribution Recommendation Created).

**Notifications Produced:** BN-S-070 (Distribution Recommendation Created) — on creation or material revision.

**Idempotency:** Re-evaluation with the same inputs produces the same recommendation.

**Concurrency:** Recommendations for different requirements are processed independently.

**Exceptional Conditions:** If no feasible movement exists, the recommendation is marked as Infeasible with documented constraints.

**Postconditions:** An Active Distribution Recommendation exists.  BN-S-070 published if created or materially revised.

**Traceability:** Owned by SE-S-080.  Invoked by FS-S-080.  Publishes BN-S-070.

#### SE-S-081 – Distribution Plan

**Business Intent**
Publish the authoritative, versioned distribution baseline for a planning cycle—composed of the current Distribution Recommendations, not re-calculated from scratch.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains the published distribution plan version series for a Planning Scope and Planning Cycle. Each version is a snapshot of the current Active Distribution Recommendations at publication time, together with aggregate metrics, risk signals, and recovery opportunities. The Distribution Plan is not another planning calculation; it is the published, authoritative baseline composed of the current Distribution Recommendations.

**Identity**
Planning Scope (SE-C-010) + Planning Cycle + Version.

**Semantic Ownership**

| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| Primary Consumers    | Distribution Execution, Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality, Learn From Supply |

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Manage Distribution (CA-S-008) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The authoritative, versioned distribution baseline for a Planning Scope and planning cycle. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Compose current Distribution Recommendations into a published distribution baseline. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per Planning Scope and Planning Cycle. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Distribution Execution (external — shipment creation), Explain Supply Decisions, Evaluate Supply Quality, Learn From Supply. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |
| **Supersedes** | The previous Published version for the same Planning Scope and Planning Cycle. |
| **Superseded By** | A newer Published version for the same Planning Scope and Planning Cycle. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | Exactly one Published Distribution Plan exists for a given Planning Scope and Planning Cycle. The plan is a snapshot of Active Distribution Recommendations at publication time; it does not recompute them. A Published plan is immutable. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall use the plan as the authoritative distribution baseline. Execution systems generate shipments from the plan; planning capabilities use it for evaluation and learning. |
| **Known Limitations** | The plan is a snapshot, not a live view. Recommendations may change after publication; those changes are reflected in the next plan version. |
| **Version Expectations** | Published on the planning cycle cadence. Superseded versions are retained permanently. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Published on the cadence defined by the Distribution Policy. |

| Stability Summary | Average Stability Score, Resources with high movement volatility | Derived | Enterprise-level stability assessment. |
| Evidence | Source Distribution Recommendation IDs, Publication Timestamp | Mandatory | Evidence lineage. |

#### SE-S-090 – Supply Change Assessment

**Business Intent**
Maintain the enterprise’s continuously current awareness of what has changed in the supply ecosystem—capturing the current change state, evidence, confidence, materiality, and the historical evolution of changes over time.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains the current supply change assessment for one monitored supply entity and change type. It captures what changed (current change state), why the enterprise believes it changed (evidence and confidence), whether the change is material to planning (materiality), whether it was planned or unplanned, its temporal context, its lifecycle stage, and the correlated chain of related changes. It also preserves the immutable history of how the change evolved from initial observation through corroboration, confirmation, resolution, and archival. Multiple concurrent changes on the same entity are supported through distinct change types.

**Identity**
Supply Entity Type + Supply Entity Identifier + Change Type. One assessment per monitored entity per change type. Examples: Supplier S1 + Quantity Reduction, Resource R3 + Capacity Reduction, Lane L4 + Disruption. Entity types map to Enterprise Semantic Objects (Supplier SE-C-004, Physical Resource SE-C-007, Transportation Lane SE-C-008, etc.).

**Semantic Ownership**

| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Sense Supply Changes (CA-S-009) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Sense Supply Changes (CA-S-009) |
| Primary Consumers    | Detect Supply Exceptions, Plan Supply, Evaluate Supply Quality, Learn From Supply, Explain Supply Decisions |

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Sense Supply Changes (CA-S-009) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The continuously maintained awareness of a supply change for a monitored entity and change type. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Detect, corroborate, and confirm supply changes; assess materiality and confidence. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per monitored supply entity and change type. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Detect Supply Exceptions, Plan Supply, Evaluate Supply Quality, Learn From Supply. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | At any moment, exactly one current assessment exists per monitored entity and change type. The current change state reflects the latest understanding based on all available signals. Change History Events are immutable. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall treat the assessment as the authoritative record of what has changed. It does not determine whether the change constitutes an exception. |
| **Known Limitations** | The assessment is a point-in-time interpretation. Confidence may be low initially and increase with corroboration. |
| **Version Expectations** | Continuously maintained. History preserved. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Updated upon signal receipt or scheduled re-evaluation. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Detect Supply Exceptions, Plan Supply, Evaluate Supply Quality, Learn From Supply. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**

| State | Description | Transition Trigger |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| No Change | Baseline state; no change detected. | Initial or after resolution. |
| Observed | Signal received; not yet corroborated. | Signal received; confidence Low or Unconfirmed. |
| Corroborated | Corroborated by independent source. | Second independent signal. |
| Confirmed | Change confirmed; materiality assessed. | Sufficient evidence; materiality assessed. |
| Resolved | Change resolved or no longer relevant. | Underlying condition returns to baseline or becomes irrelevant. |
| Archived | Retained for audit; no longer monitored. | After retention period following resolution. |

- **Terminal States:** Archived.
- **History Preservation:** All lifecycle transitions preserved.

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Type | Description |
|----------|-------------|------|-------------|
| Identity | Supply Entity Type + Supply Entity Identifier + Change Type | Mandatory | Unique identity. |
| Current Change State | Change State, Change Description, Change Magnitude, Change Direction | Derived | Current understanding. |
| Change Classification | Planned / Unplanned | Derived | Whether expected or unexpected. |
| Materiality | Material to Planning / Non-Material / Unassessed | Derived | Planning materiality. |
| Temporal Context | Occurrence Time, Detection Time, Effective Time, Expected Duration, Actual Resolution Time | Mandatory | Four timestamps. |
| Evidence | Source Signals, Corroborating Signals, Signal Summary | Mandatory | Why the enterprise believes the change occurred. |
| Assessment Confidence | Confirmed, High, Medium, Low, Unconfirmed | Derived | Confidence in assessment. |
| Correlated Changes | References to other Supply Change Assessments | Optional | Related changes. |
| Change History | Chronological list of Change History Events | Derived | Immutable record. |

**Relationships**

| Relationship | Target Object | Cardinality | Description |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| monitors change for | Supply Entity (generic) | Many-to-One | The entity being monitored (e.g., Supplier SE-C-004, Physical Resource SE-C-007, Transportation Lane SE-C-008). |
| correlated with | Supply Change Assessment (SE-S-090) | Many-to-Many | Related changes. |

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Type | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| Semantic Dependency | None directly. References enterprise entities generically. |
| Supply Domain Dependency | None. |

**Invariants**
- At any moment, exactly one current assessment exists per monitored entity and change type.
- Current Change State is derived from latest Change History Event.
- Change History Events are immutable.
- Materiality assessment is scoped to planning relevance.

**Traceability**
- **Business Owner:** CA-S-009.
- **Produced By:** AB-S-080.
- **Referenced By:** FS-S-080.
- **Governed By:** BR-S-170–178 and PO-S-100.
- **Upward:** Constitution CN-003, CN-004; ARS §3, §4, §16.

#### AB-S-080 — Manage Supply Change

**Purpose**
For a given monitored supply entity and change type, invoke the Supply Change Assessment (BA-S-060), determine the resulting lifecycle state from the assessment, persist the state transition and assessment evidence, and publish the appropriate events.

**Business Intent**
Maintain the enterprise's continuously current awareness of supply changes by delegating change assessment to BA-S-060 and managing the lifecycle of the Supply Change Assessment based on the assessment output.

**Trigger**
Incoming supply signal or scheduled re-evaluation.

**Preconditions**
Monitored entity is registered for change detection. Supply Change Policy (PO-S-100) is current.

**Semantic Preconditions**
- The monitored supply entity exists in the enterprise (e.g., Supplier SE-C-004, Physical Resource SE-C-007, Transportation Lane SE-C-008).
- The change type is recognised per PO-S-100.

**Business Behaviour**
Normalise the incoming signal into the canonical change representation. Invoke BA-S-060 (Assess Supply Change) to evaluate materiality, confidence, and evidence. Apply lifecycle transition rules per PO-S-100 to determine the next state. Persist the state transition, evidence, and change history.

**State Transitions**
- **Required Input State:** Any lifecycle stage.
- **Produced Output State:** Updated per lifecycle (e.g., No Change → Observed → Corroborated → Confirmed → Resolved → Archived). Change History Event appended if state transitions.

**Business Transaction**
Protects Supply Change Assessment aggregate. Atomic update of current state, history, and assessment evidence.

**Decisions Invoked**
None (the lifecycle determination is a deterministic consequence of the BA-S-060 assessment and PO-S-100; no business choice is made).

**Rules Enforced**
BR-S-170–178.

**Policies Referenced**
PO-S-100 (Supply Change Policy).

**Algorithms Invoked**
BA-S-060 (Assess Supply Change).

**Events Published**
EV-S-080 (Supply Change Assessment Updated).

**Notifications Produced**
BN-S-080 (Supply Change Assessment Updated) — on state transition per PO-S-100.

**Idempotency**
Re-evaluation with the same signals produces the same outcome.

**Concurrency**
Assessments for different entity-change type combinations processed independently.

**Exceptional Conditions**
If signals are contradictory, confidence is reduced and the assessment may remain in Observed state until corroborated.

**Postconditions**
The Supply Change Assessment reflects the latest enterprise understanding. BN-S-080 published if state changed.

**Traceability**
Owned by SE-S-090. Invoked by FS-S-080. Invokes BA-S-060. Publishes EV-S-080, BN-S-080.

#### SE-S-100 – Supply Quality Assessment

**Business Intent**
Publish an authoritative, periodic enterprise assessment of supply system performance against governed objectives—evaluating how well the enterprise achieved its intended supply outcomes, not merely reporting metrics.

Provides the authoritative supply interpretation for comparison against planned outcomes.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains the published supply quality assessment version series for an assessment scope, planning horizon, and evaluation period. Each version evaluates each performance dimension against governed objectives, produces enterprise judgments (not merely metrics), records the assessment context, supports comparison with prior periods and targets, and provides the evidence and rationale for every judgment. It is not a KPI dashboard or a metrics report; it is the enterprise's governed evaluation of supply performance.

**Identity:** Assessment Scope (Governed Identifier from PO-S-110 assessment scope enumeration) + Planning Horizon (Governed Identifier: Operational, Tactical, Strategic) + Evaluation Period (Planning Period reference or explicit date range) + Version (monotonically increasing integer).

**Assessment Scope Definition:** A governed identifier representing the enterprise boundary for the assessment (e.g., “Enterprise”, “Business Unit: EMEA”, “Product Family: A”).  The allowed values are defined in PO-S-110 and may be extended by governance.  For the initial release, the mandatory scopes are “Enterprise” (for all-encompassing assessments) and one scope per declared Business Unit.

**Evaluation Period Type:** A date range with a start timestamp and end timestamp (both SE-C-022).  The period must align with the Planning Horizon cadence (e.g., a calendar week for Operational, a calendar month for Tactical).

| Semantic Authority   | Evaluate Supply Quality (CA-S-010) |

| Operational Capability | Evaluate Supply Quality (CA-S-010) |
| Primary Consumers    | Learn From Supply, Explain Supply Decisions, Detect Supply Exceptions, Supply Planners and Managers |

| **Authority Scope** | Per scope, horizon, and evaluation period. |

| Section | Value |

| **Business Guarantees** | Exactly one Published Supply Quality Assessment exists for a given scope, horizon, and period. A Published assessment is immutable. Every dimensional judgment is supported by evidence references. The Overall Assessment is derived from dimensional assessments according to governed composition rules. Assessment Context is recorded when it materially affects interpretation. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall treat the assessment as the authoritative enterprise judgment of supply performance. It is not a raw metrics report. |

The Authoritative Judgment and Trend are set by DE-S-091; the Recommended Classification and metrics are produced by BA-S-070. |

#### AB-S-090 — Publish Supply Quality Assessment

**Purpose**
Compute the supply quality evaluation for each performance dimension according to the Supply Quality Policy, derive the overall assessment, record assessment context, comparators, confidence, and rationale, and publish the authoritative assessment for the evaluation period.

**Business Intent**
Provide the authoritative periodic enterprise judgment of supply performance.

**Trigger**
Scheduled per Supply Quality Policy (PO-S-110).

**Preconditions**
All mandatory source artifacts available for the evaluation period. Supply Quality Policy current.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- All referenced source assessments (SE-S-001, SE-S-020, SE-S-032, SE-S-041, SE-S-052, SE-S-061, SE-S-071, SE-S-081, SE-S-090) are Published and current for the evaluation period.
- Supply Quality Policy (PO-S-110) is current and defines the governed dimensions, thresholds, and composition rules.
- The Assessment Scope and Evaluation Period are valid per PO-S-110.

**Business Behaviour**

1. Load the supply quality objectives and governed performance dimensions from PO-S-110.
2. For each performance dimension defined by the policy:
   - Invoke BA-S-070 (Evaluate Supply Quality Dimensions) to produce a Dimensional Quality Evaluation, including evaluated metrics, objective deviation, recommended classification, recommended trend, and evaluation confidence.
   - Invoke DE-S-091 (Evaluate Supply Performance) to determine the authoritative judgment and trend by applying PO-S-110 thresholds and any declared context to the BA-S-070 evaluation.
   - Record the authoritative judgment, trend, evidence, and context in the assessment.
3. After all dimensions are evaluated:
   - Invoke BA-S-071 (Derive Overall Supply Quality Assessment) to synthesise the overall judgment from the dimensional authoritative judgments per PO-S-110 composition rules.
   - Record the overall assessment, rationale, and confidence.
4. Invoke DE-S-092 (Publish Supply Quality Assessment) to determine publication readiness.
5. If Publish: transition to Published, supersede previous version, publish BN-S-090.

**State Transitions**
- **Required Input State:** None (creation) or Draft.
- **Produced Output State:** Published (previous → Superseded).

**Business Transaction**
Protects Supply Quality Assessment aggregate.

**Decisions Invoked**
DE-S-091 (per dimension), DE-S-092 (publish).

#### SE-S-110 – Supply Exception Assessment

**Business Intent**
Maintain the authoritative enterprise record that one or more governed supply conditions have been breached, creating a situation that requires attention—not merely that a risk exists, but that a policy has been violated or a threshold crossed.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains the lifecycle of a single supply exception—a bounded enterprise situation where a governed supply policy has been breached. Each exception is an enterprise judgment that attention is required; it is not an event, a notification, or an alert. An exception is identified by the specific policy violation and the scope of its impact, persisting until the underlying conditions return to compliance. If the same policy is breached again later for the same scope, a new exception with a new identity is created. Risk evidence is consumed from existing assessments; the exception exists because a policy has been violated, not merely because risk exists.

**Semantic Ownership**

| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Detect Supply Exceptions (CA-S-011) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Detect Supply Exceptions (CA-S-011) |
| Primary Consumers    | Explain Supply Decisions, Learn From Supply, Supply Planners and Managers |

**Identity:**  
- **Supply Exception Identifier:** Globally unique, assigned at creation. Immutable.  
- **Business Identity:** Governed Policy Reference (the `PO-xxx` identifier of the violated policy) + Exception Scope (governed identifier from the PO-S-120 scope enumeration) + Exception Type (governed identifier from the PO-S-120 exception taxonomy).  This defines “the same exception” over time.

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Detect Supply Exceptions (CA-S-011) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The authoritative record of a governed supply policy violation. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Detect policy violations, assess severity, and maintain the exception lifecycle. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per policy, scope, and exception type. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Explain Supply Decisions, Learn From Supply, Supply Planners and Managers. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | Every exception is traceable to a specific governed policy and rule. Risk evidence is consumed from existing assessments; no separate risk assessment aggregate is created. The lifecycle state reflects the current status; resolved exceptions are immutable. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall interpret the exception as the authoritative record that a governed boundary has been breached. It does not prescribe actions. |
| **Known Limitations** | The exception records the violation, not the full operational context. |
| **Version Expectations** | Persists until resolved. Retained permanently. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Updated as evidence changes. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Explain Supply Decisions, Learn From Supply, Planners and Managers. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**

| State | Description | Transition Trigger |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| Detected | Evidence suggests a policy violation. | Automatic detection or manual flagging. |
| Confirmed | Policy violation confirmed; authoritative record. | Sufficient evidence; severity assessed. |
| Resolved | Conditions returned to compliance. | Evidence confirms compliance. |

- **Permitted Transitions:** Detected → Confirmed → Resolved; Detected → Resolved (false positive).
- **Terminal States:** Resolved (immutable; retained permanently).

**Information Model**

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Type | Description |
|----------|-------------|------|-------------|
| Identity | Supply Exception Identifier | Mandatory | Globally unique enterprise identifier. |
| Identity | Governed Policy Reference + Exception Scope + Exception Type | Mandatory | Business identity defining “the same exception”. |
| Exception Classification | Exception Type (governed identifier) | Mandatory | Category of breached policy from PO-S-120 taxonomy. |
| Triggering Evidence | References to Supply Change Assessments, Supply Quality Assessment findings, risk evidence from position assessments | Mandatory | Evidence that collectively constitutes the exception. |
| Governing Policy | Specific governed policy and rule violated (PO-xxx, BR-xxx) | Mandatory | Traceable to the policy and rule that was breached. |
| Severity Assessment | Business Impact, Urgency, Scope, Potential Impact, Current Impact | Derived | Multi-dimensional severity assessment. |
| Exception Horizon | Immediate, Short-term, Medium-term, Future, Uncertain | Derived | When impact is expected. |
| Correlated Exceptions | References to other Supply Exception Assessments | Optional | Related exceptions. |
| Lifecycle State | Detected, Confirmed, Resolved | Mandatory | Current state. |
| Evidence History | Chronological list of Evidence Events | Derived | Immutable record of state transitions and evidence updates. |
| Traceability | Detection Timestamp, Confirmation Timestamp, Resolution Timestamp | Mandatory | Temporal context. |

**Relationships**

| Relationship | Target Object | Cardinality | Description |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| references evidence from | Supply Change Assessment (SE-S-090) | Many-to-Many | Changes that triggered detection. |
| references evidence from | Supply Quality Assessment (SE-S-100) | Many-to-Many | Quality context. |
| references evidence from | Inventory Position Assessment (SE-S-030) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |
| references evidence from | Capacity Position Assessment (SE-S-040) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |
| references evidence from | Supplier Commitment Assessment (SE-S-051) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |
| references evidence from | Production Schedule (SE-S-070) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |
| references evidence from | Distribution Recommendation (SE-S-080) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |
| references evidence from | Procurement Recommendation (SE-S-060) | Many-to-Many | Operational evidence. |

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Type | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| Supply Domain Dependency | SE-S-090, SE-S-100, SE-S-030, SE-S-040, SE-S-051, SE-S-070, SE-S-080, SE-S-060. |

**Invariants**
- Exception shall not be created unless a governed policy has been breached.
- Every exception must reference the specific governed policy and rule.
- Business identity defines "the same exception" over time.
- Risk evidence consumed from existing assessments; no duplication.
- Resolved exceptions are immutable.

**Traceability**
- **Business Owner:** CA-S-011. Produced By: AB-S-100. Referenced by FS-S-100. Governed by BR-S-210–220 and PO-S-120.
- **Upward:** Constitution CN-003, CN-004; ARS §3, §4, §16.

### AB-S-100 — Evaluate Supply Exception

**Purpose:** For a given set of correlated changes, performance signals, and risk evidence, invoke the Supply Exception Assessment (BA-S-080), determine the resulting lifecycle state from the assessment, persist the state transition and assessment evidence, and publish the appropriate events.

**Business Intent:** Maintain the authoritative lifecycle of supply exceptions by delegating exception assessment to BA-S-080 and managing the lifecycle based on the assessment output.

**Trigger:** Scheduled evaluation, or when upstream assessments change materially.

**Preconditions:** Exception Detection Policy (PO-S-120) current. Governed supply policies available. Evidence from upstream assessments accessible.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- The governed policy referenced by the exception identity exists and is active (e.g., PO-S-032, PO-S-050, PO-S-060).
- All upstream assessments providing evidence (SE-S-090, SE-S-100, SE-S-030, SE-S-040, SE-S-051, SE-S-070, SE-S-080, SE-S-060) are Published and current for the relevant scope and period.
- Exception Detection Policy (PO-S-120) is current.

**Business Behaviour:**  
Gather correlated evidence from the relevant upstream assessments for the governed policy and scope. Invoke BA-S-080 (Evaluate Supply Exception) to produce a structured exception assessment, including whether an exception exists, its severity, horizon, and correlation context. Based on the assessment output and the transition rules governed by PO-S-120, determine the resulting lifecycle state (Detected, Confirmed, or Resolved). Persist the state transition and assessment evidence. Publish BN-S-100 if the state or severity changed per PO-S-120.

**State Transitions:**
- **Required Input State:** None (new exception), Detected, or Confirmed.
- **Produced Output State:** Detected, Confirmed, or Resolved per PO-S-120.

**Business Transaction:** Protects Supply Exception Assessment aggregate. Atomic update.

**Decisions Invoked:** None (lifecycle determined by BA-S-080 and PO-S-120).

**Rules Enforced:** BR-S-210–214.

**Policies Referenced:** PO-S-120 (Exception Detection Policy).

**Algorithms Invoked:** BA-S-080 (Evaluate Supply Exception).

**Events Published:** EV-S-100 (Supply Exception Assessment Updated).

**Notifications Produced:** BN-S-100 (Supply Exception Assessment Updated) — published on state transition or severity change.

**Idempotency:** Re-evaluation with same evidence and policy produces same outcome.

**Concurrency:** Exceptions for different policy-scope-type combinations are independent.

**Exceptional Conditions:** None beyond standard state transition rules.

**Postconditions:** Exception lifecycle reflects current state. BN-S-100 published if state changed.

**Traceability:** Owned by SE-S-110. Invoked by FS-S-100. Publishes BN-S-100.

### SE-S-120 – Supply Explanation

**Business Intent**
Provide an immutable, auditable enterprise record of the reasoning behind any supply intelligence conclusion—composing the evidence, decisions, policies, and assumptions that were already preserved when that conclusion was reached.

**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains an immutable explanation for one supply artifact (a Supply Plan version, Inventory Health Assessment, Capacity Position Assessment, Supplier Commitment, Procurement Recommendation, Production Schedule, Distribution Recommendation, Supply Quality Assessment, Supply Exception Assessment, or any other enterprise conclusion with preserved evidence). The explanation is a structured composition of the decision evidence, governing policies, assumptions, and traceability already preserved at the source. It may be formally revised, withdrawn, or superseded independently of the explained artifact.

**Semantic Ownership**

| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Explain Supply Decisions (CA-S-012) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Explain Supply Decisions (CA-S-012) |
| Primary Consumers    | Learn From Supply, Planners and Auditors, AI Copilot |

**Identity**
Supply Explanation Identifier, globally unique, assigned at creation. Immutable.

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Explain Supply Decisions (CA-S-012) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The immutable, structured explanation of a supply intelligence conclusion. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Compose preserved evidence into an auditable explanation record. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per explanation. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Learn From Supply, Planners and Auditors, AI Copilot. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | Given the same artifact, evidence versions, policy versions, and template, the Structured Reasoning must be identical. The explanation references historical versions of all contributing evidence. Once created, an explanation shall never be silently modified. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall interpret the explanation as the authoritative reasoning behind the conclusion. AI may render it; the structure is deterministic. |
| **Known Limitations** | The explanation composes existing knowledge; it does not invent new reasoning. |
| **Version Expectations** | May be revised, withdrawn, or superseded independently of the explained artifact. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Created on demand or automatically per policy. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Learn From Supply, Planners and Auditors, AI Copilot. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**

| State | Description | Transition Trigger |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| Active | Current authoritative explanation. | Created on demand or automatically. |
| Revised | Replaced by new explanation; original retained. | New explanation created. |
| Withdrawn | Formally withdrawn; retained as historical record. | Governance determines reasoning incomplete/incorrect. |
| Superseded | Replaced by newer explanation using improved template. | New explanation created with later template/policy set. |

- **Terminal States:** (all states except Active are terminal for that version).
- **History Preservation:** All versions retained permanently.

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Type | Description |
|----------|-------------|------|-------------|
| Identity | Supply Explanation Identifier | Mandatory | Globally unique, immutable. |
| Explained Artifact | Artifact Type, Artifact Identifier (with version) | Mandatory | The conclusion being explained. |
| Structured Reasoning | Canonical composition of evidence, decisions, policies, assumptions | Derived | Deterministic reasoning structure. |
| Decision Trace | Causal chain of decisions and assessments | Derived | How one conclusion led to another. |
| Policy Trace | Chain from decision through policies, rules, to Constitution | Derived | Governance influence. |
| Negative Explanation | Explanation of why a decision/exception was deliberately not made | Optional | Supports explainability of inaction. |
| Explanation Confidence | Inherited Evidence Confidence, Evidence Completeness, Evidence Consistency | Derived | Composite confidence. |
| Explanation Provenance | Evidence Version Set, Policy Version Set, Template Version, Generation Timestamp | Mandatory | Snapshot of reasoning inputs. |
| Source Evidence | References to specific artifact versions, policies, assumptions | Mandatory | Full traceability. |
| Traceability | ARS Traceability Chain, Revision History | Mandatory | Lineage. |

**Relationships**

| Relationship | Target Object | Cardinality | Description |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| explains conclusion of | Any Supply Intelligence artifact | Many-to-One | The artifact being explained. |
| references evidence from | All Supply Intelligence capabilities | Many-to-Many | Preserved evidence. |

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Type | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| Supply Domain Dependency | All Supply artifacts that produce explanations. |

**Invariants**
- Given identical inputs, Structured Reasoning must be identical.
- Explanation must reference historical versions of evidence.
- Once created, never silently modified.

**Traceability**
- **Business Owner:** CA-S-012. Produced By: AB-S-110. Referenced by FS-S-110. Governed by BR-S-230–238 and PO-S-130.
- **Upward:** Constitution CN-003, CN-004; ARS §3, §4, §16.

#### SE-S-130 – Supply Learning

**Business Intent**
Provide an authoritative, immutable enterprise record of what the enterprise has concluded about a recurring supply phenomenon—what it means, whether it warrants change, and with what confidence—based on systematic analysis of historical outcomes, patterns, and evidence.


**Enterprise Meaning**
The aggregate root that maintains an immutable learning record for one recurring supply phenomenon. Each learning captures the observed pattern, the enterprise's conclusion about what it means (the Learning), the evidence supporting that conclusion, one or more Improvement Opportunities that derive from it, and the enterprise's decision outcome (Accepted, Rejected, or Deferred). The pattern is supporting evidence; the Learning is the identity. If the enterprise's understanding of the phenomenon itself evolves materially, a new Supply Learning is created.

**Semantic Ownership**
| Ownership Dimension | Value |
|---------------------|-------|
| Semantic Authority   | Learn From Supply (CA-S-013) |
| Steward Domain       | Supply Intelligence |
| Operational Capability | Learn From Supply (CA-S-013) |
| Primary Consumers    | Planning Governance, Plan Supply, Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Schedule Production, Manage Distribution |

**Identity**
Enterprise Learning Identifier (globally unique) + the Learning statement itself defines the business identity.

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Learn From Supply (CA-S-013) |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The immutable enterprise learning record. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Record conclusions about recurring supply phenomena and their improvement implications. |
| **Authority Scope** | Per learning. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Planning Governance, Plan Supply, Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Schedule Production, Manage Distribution, Future planning cycles. |
| **Non-Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | Every learning is supported by evidence of recurrence. Pattern Confidence and Intervention Confidence are distinct and independently assessed. Rejected learnings are permanently preserved. Learnings are evaluated from an enterprise-system perspective. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers shall treat the learning as the enterprise's conclusion. Improvement Opportunities are derived suggestions, not mandates. |
| **Known Limitations** | The learning is based on historical evidence; future conditions may differ. |
| **Version Expectations** | Created as immutable; never modified. New understanding creates a new learning. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Created when sufficient evidence accumulates. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Planning Governance, all downstream planning capabilities. |

**Lifecycle Specification Contract**
No state transitions. Created as immutable. Learning Outcome recorded at creation.

**Information Model**

| Category | Information | Description |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Identity | Enterprise Learning Identifier, Learning Statement | Unique identity. |
| Observed Pattern | Description, Recurrence evidence, Pattern Scope | The phenomenon that triggered learning. |
| Enterprise Learning | The enterprise's conclusion | The identity of the learning. |
| Pattern Confidence | Confidence that pattern genuinely exists | Based on recurrence and evidence. |
| Improvement Opportunity | One or more proposed improvements | Derived from the learning. |
| Intervention Confidence | Confidence that acting will produce benefit | Distinct from Pattern Confidence. |
| Learning Outcome | Accepted, Rejected, Deferred | Enterprise decision. |
| Evidence Summary | References to historical records across multiple periods | Evidence must span multiple periods/events. |
| Learning Scope | Enterprise, Business Unit, Product Family, Supplier Network, Distribution Network | Scope of observation. |
| Time Horizon | Period over which pattern observed | Learning spans longer horizons. |
| Traceability | Generation Timestamp, Source Evidence Version Set, Learning Policy Version | Provenance. |

**Relationships**

| Relationship | Target Object | Cardinality | Description |
|--------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| references evidence from | All Supply Intelligence capabilities | Many-to-Many | Historical evidence. |

**Dependencies**

| Dependency Type | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| Supply Domain Dependency | All Supply assessments, plans, recommendations, schedules, explanations. |

**Invariants**
- Learning must be supported by evidence of recurrence.
- Learning statement defines business identity.
- Pattern Confidence and Intervention Confidence distinct.
- Rejected learnings preserved.

**Traceability**
- **Business Owner:** CA-S-013. Produced By: AB-S-120. Referenced by FS-S-120. Governed by BR-S-250–258 and PO-S-140.
- **Upward:** Constitution CN-003, CN-004; ARS §3, §4, §16.

#### AB-S-120 — Record Supply Learning

**Purpose**
Analyze historical supply outcomes, patterns, and evidence across the domain according to the Learning Policy, and record an immutable Supply Learning when the evidence supports a conclusion about a recurring phenomenon.

**Business Intent**
Derive and record enterprise learning from historical evidence.

**Trigger**
Scheduled per Learning Policy or when sufficient new evidence accumulates.

**Preconditions**
Historical evidence available across the domain. Learning Policy current.

**Semantic Preconditions**
- All referenced historical evidence (assessments, plans, explanations) is available and immutable.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- Historical evidence from across the Supply Intelligence domain is available and spans the minimum periods defined by PO-S-140.
- Learning Policy (PO-S-140) is current.

**Business Behaviour**
Invoke BA-S-100 (Derive Supply Learning) to analyse evidence and produce candidate learnings. For each candidate meeting recurrence and evidence thresholds, record an immutable Supply Learning with Pattern Confidence, Intervention Confidence, and Improvement Opportunities. Governance decision (Accept/Reject/Defer) is recorded externally.

**State Transitions**
- **Required Input State:** None (creation).
- **Produced Output State:** Created (immutable).

**Business Transaction**
Protects Supply Learning aggregate.

**Decisions Invoked**
DE-S-121 (Evaluate Supply Learning).

**Rules Enforced**
BR-S-250–253.

**Policies Referenced**
PO-S-140 (Learning Policy).

**Algorithms Invoked**
BA-S-100 (Derive Supply Learning).

**Events Published**
EV-S-120 (Supply Learning Recorded).

**Notifications Produced**
BN-S-120 (Supply Learning Recorded) — per learning.

**Idempotency**
Re-analysis with same evidence produces same learning; duplicates not created.

**Concurrency**
Analyses for different learning scopes independent.

**Postconditions**

Owned by SE-S-130. Invoked by FS-S-120. Publishes BN-S-120.


### AB-S-121 — Record Learning Outcome

**Purpose:** Record the enterprise’s governance decision on a Supply Learning.

**Business Intent:** Update the learning with the accepted, rejected, or deferred outcome determined by governance.

**Trigger:** Governance decision is made on a candidate Supply Learning.

**Preconditions:** A Supply Learning (SE-S-130) exists and is immutable except for the Learning Outcome. The governance outcome (Accept, Reject, Defer) is authorised.

**Semantic Preconditions:**
- The Supply Learning (SE-S-130) exists and is in the Created state.
- The governance authority has made a decision per PO-S-140.

**Business Behaviour:** Set the `Learning Outcome` attribute of the Supply Learning to the authorised value. The learning record remains immutable otherwise.

**State Transitions:**
- **Required Input State:** Created (immutable learning, outcome not yet set).
- **Produced Output State:** Created (outcome appended; the learning itself does not change state).

**Business Transaction:** Protects Supply Learning aggregate. Atomic update of Learning Outcome.

**Decisions Invoked:** None (governance decision made externally).

**Rules Enforced:** BR-S-256 (Rejected learnings preserved), BR-S-258 (immutability – outcome is the only allowed update).

**Policies Referenced:** PO-S-140.

**Algorithms Invoked:** None.

**Events Published:** EV-S-121 (Supply Learning Outcome Recorded).

**Notifications Produced:** BN-S-121 (Supply Learning Outcome Recorded).

**Idempotency:** Recording the same outcome twice has no additional effect.

**Concurrency:** Outcome recorded once per learning.

**Exceptional Conditions:** If the learning already has a recorded outcome, the operation is rejected.

**Postconditions:** Learning Outcome is recorded. BN-S-121 published.

**Traceability:** Owned by SE-S-130. Invoked by governance process (external trigger).

### 4.3.6 Supply Enumerations

The following governed enumerations are used across Supply capabilities.

# Chapter 5 — Capability Model

## 5.1 Understand Supply — CA‑S‑001

**Business Intent**  
Interpret the latest Enterprise Picture (SE‑C‑021) and detected supply change signals (SE‑S‑090) into the enterprise’s authoritative supply interpretation—the Supply Understanding (SE‑S‑001)—so that downstream planning capabilities act on a single, governed view of supply health, risk, and confidence.

**Enterprise Question**  
What supply does the enterprise truly have, and what does the current supply situation mean for planning?

**Authoritative Enterprise Output**  
The Published Supply Understanding (SE‑S‑001).

**Position in Enterprise Reasoning**

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Consumes** | Enterprise Picture (SE‑C‑021), Supply Change Assessment (SE‑S‑090), Enterprise Policies (PO‑S‑011, PO‑S‑012). |
| **Produces** | Supply Understanding (SE‑S‑001) – the authoritative interpretation of current supply health, risk, and confidence. |
| **Feeds** | Plan Supply, Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Promise Intelligence, Scenario Intelligence. All consumption is within the **same planning cycle** (the Understanding is the interpretive baseline for the current planning run). |

**Authority Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Owner** | Supply Intelligence Domain |
| **Authoritative Representation** | The governed definition of how the enterprise interprets current supply health, risk, and confidence. |
| **Business Responsibility** | Interpret the Enterprise Picture and supply change signals into the Supply Understanding; publish materially changed versions as the single interpretive source for downstream planning. |
| **Authority Scope** | Enterprise‑wide, all Planning Scopes. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Plan Supply, Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Promise Intelligence, Scenario Intelligence. |
| **Non‑Intended Consumers** | None. |
| **Supersedes** | None. |
| **Superseded By** | None. |

**Consumer Specification Contract**

| Section | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Business Guarantees** | Exactly one Published Supply Understanding exists per Planning Scope at any moment. Every interpretation dimension is traceable to the specific Enterprise Picture version and Supply Change Assessments used. Only published evidence contributes. Materiality thresholds prevent over‑versioning while ensuring significant changes are always published. |
| **Required Interpretation** | Consumers must treat the Published Understanding as the exclusive interpretive baseline for current supply. It does not contain raw operational data; for actual inventory positions, capacity statuses, or supplier commitments, consumers must reference the Enterprise Picture or the assessments produced by downstream capabilities. |
| **Known Limitations** | The Understanding is a point‑in‑time interpretation. It does not include demand forecasts, supply plans, or projections. It is not a substitute for the detailed operational assessments produced by Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, or Collaborate with Suppliers. |
| **Version Expectations** | Only Published versions are authoritative. Every Published version replaces the previous one. Drafts are internal. |
| **Freshness Expectations** | Updated upon material change in the Enterprise Picture or supply change signals, and published in near‑real‑time. A periodic refresh may also occur per PO‑S‑012. Consumers should expect near‑real‑time notification (BN‑S‑001) on publication. |
| **Intended Consumers** | Plan Supply, Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Promise Intelligence, Scenario Intelligence. |
| **Non‑Intended Consumers** | None. |

**Business Guarantees**
- Exactly one Published Supply Understanding exists for each Planning Scope at any moment.
- Every interpretation dimension carries traceable evidence references to the Enterprise Picture version and Supply Change Assessments used.
- Only published evidence contributes to the Understanding.
- Materiality thresholds prevent over‑versioning while ensuring significant interpretation changes are always published.

- SE‑S‑010 – Supply Data Record (received and evaluated, but the Understanding itself does not consume raw data; the Enterprise Picture does)

## 5.2 Plan Supply — CA-S-002

**Business Intent:** Produce the enterprise's authoritative, feasible, and balanced supply plan that establishes the planning baseline for all downstream supply capabilities.

Before Plan Supply executes, the enterprise possesses independent understanding of demand (from Demand Intelligence) and current supply interpretation (from Understand Supply), but no unified understanding of how future demand is expected to be satisfied. After Plan Supply, the enterprise possesses a single authoritative enterprise understanding — the published Supply Plan — that specifies how demand will be met through production, procurement, and transfers, respecting all constraints and balancing service, cost, and risk. This plan becomes the planning baseline that all downstream supply capabilities consume rather than independently determining supply requirements.

**Enterprise Question:** What is the feasible, balanced plan to satisfy demand across the supply network?

**Owned Semantic Objects:** SE-S-020 (Supply Plan).

**Enterprise Dependencies**

Plan Supply transforms multiple sources of enterprise knowledge into a unified supply plan. These dependencies are categorized by their enterprise nature.

**Enterprise Understanding** (consumed from other capabilities — authoritative published knowledge)

| Dependency | Role in Plan Supply |
|------------|---------------------|
Supply Understanding (SE-S-001) | Provides the enterprise's authoritative interpretation of current supply health, risk, and confidence. Plan Supply uses this interpretive baseline to project how the current supply situation will evolve and to determine what additional supply actions are needed.
| Demand Forecast (from Demand Intelligence) | Represents the enterprise's authoritative projection of future demand. Plan Supply balances this demand against available and planned supply to determine what must be produced, procured, or transferred. |

**Enterprise Master Data** (stable enterprise definitions — define *what* is being planned)

| Dependency | Role in Plan Supply |
|------------|---------------------|
| Product (from Master Data) | Provides the enterprise definition of every planned item and forms the planning identity used throughout supply planning. |
| Resource (from Master Data) | Provides the enterprise definition of every capacity-constrained production resource used to evaluate production feasibility. |
| Supplier (from Master Data) | Provides the enterprise definition of approved sources of procurement together with contractual planning attributes. |
| Bill of Materials (from Master Data) | Defines material consumption relationships required to translate finished-product demand into component requirements. |
| Routing (from Master Data) | Defines the sequence of operations and resource requirements required to transform materials into planned supply. |
| Transportation Lane (from Master Data) | Defines permissible material movement between locations together with planning lead times and transportation constraints. |

**Enterprise Governance** (governs *how* planning is performed)

| Dependency | Role in Plan Supply |
|------------|---------------------|
| Planning Calendar (from Master Data / Planning Governance) | Defines the enterprise planning horizon, bucket structure, and working calendar used throughout supply planning. |
| Planning Parameters (from Planning Governance) | Define the enterprise planning strategy for a Planning Scope, including horizon configuration, bucket definitions, frozen periods, sourcing priorities, lot-sizing behavior, and planning frequencies. Unlike Master Data (which defines *what* is being planned), Planning Parameters govern *how* planning is performed. Unlike Policies (which govern enterprise behavior), Planning Parameters define the operational configuration of the planning process. |
| Supply Planning Policies (PO-S-021, PO-S-022, PO-S-023) | Govern the acceptance, publication, and constraint relaxation decisions made during plan generation and evaluation. |

**Business Guarantees:**
- Exactly one Published Supply Plan exists for a given Planning Scope at any moment.
- Every Published plan satisfies all hard constraints or documents approved constraint relaxations.
- The plan covers the full planning horizon for all mandatory product-location combinations.
- All published plans are immutable and permanently retained.
- Once published, the Enterprise Supply Plan becomes the authoritative planning baseline for all downstream supply planning capabilities until superseded. Downstream capabilities consume this baseline rather than independently determining supply requirements.

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Consumes | Supply Understanding (SE‑S‑001), Demand Forecast (Demand Intelligence), Enterprise Master Data, Supply Planning Policies |
| Produces | Supply Plan (SE‑S‑020) – the authoritative, feasible, balanced plan to satisfy demand |
| Feeds | Manage Inventory, Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Schedule Production, Manage Distribution, Promise Intelligence, Scenario Intelligence. All consumption is within the **same planning cycle** (the Supply Plan is the baseline for downstream operational capabilities). |

**Capability Responsibilities**

Plan Supply executes three responsibilities that together establish the authoritative Supply Plan.

| ID | Responsibility | Business Workflow | Purpose | FS |
|----|----------------|-------------------|---------|-----|
| CR-S-005 | Balance Supply and Demand | BW-S-010 | Produce a feasible future supply understanding by balancing expected demand against available and planned supply, respecting all constraints. This is the enterprise act of reconciling what is needed with what is possible. | FS-S-010 |
| CR-S-006 | Evaluate Supply Plan | BW-S-011 | Assess whether the generated plan satisfies enterprise planning objectives and governance requirements — service levels, cost targets, capacity utilization, inventory policy compliance, and plan stability. | FS-S-011 |
| CR-S-007 | Publish Supply Plan | BW-S-012 | Establish the accepted plan as the enterprise's authoritative supply planning baseline for all downstream capabilities. Publication represents a knowledge handoff: the enterprise transitions from planning to execution, and responsibility transfers to downstream consumers. | FS-S-012 |

**Knowledge Handoff**

The Supply Plan represents a critical transition in the enterprise reasoning chain. Plan Supply consumes current supply understanding and demand projections, and produces future supply understanding. Downstream capabilities consume this baseline to develop their own specialized enterprise knowledge — inventory projections, capacity assessments, procurement recommendations, production schedules. Each capability extends the reasoning chain without redefining what has already been established.

```
Supply Understanding ───→ Supply Plan ───→ Manage Inventory
Demand Forecast               (published,       Manage Capacity
                               authoritative,    Procure Materials
                               versioned)        Schedule Production
                                                 Manage Distribution
                                                 Promise Intelligence
                                                 Scenario Intelligence
```

| EV-S-011 | Supply Plan Evaluated | AB-S-011 |

| Consumer | How the Supply Plan Is Used |
|----------|-----------------------------|
| Manage Inventory | Uses projected inventory positions to evaluate future inventory health, assess replenishment adequacy, and identify potential stockout or excess situations. Develops enterprise understanding of inventory performance against policy targets. |
| Manage Capacity | Uses planned production quantities to evaluate future resource loading against available capacity, identify capacity risks (overloads and underloads), and establish enterprise understanding of production capability sufficiency. |
| Procure Materials | Uses planned procurement quantities to develop procurement recommendations, determine order timing, and establish enterprise understanding of future purchasing requirements. |
| Schedule Production | Uses planned production quantities and capacity constraints to develop executable, sequenced production schedules at the resource level. |
| Manage Distribution | Uses planned transfers to develop distribution and replenishment plans, balancing inventory across the network. |
| Promise Intelligence | Uses the authoritative Supply Plan to evaluate Available-to-Promise and Capable-to-Promise commitments, determining whether customer orders can be fulfilled. |
| Scenario Intelligence | Uses the Supply Plan as the enterprise baseline for scenario comparison and impact analysis, evaluating how changes in assumptions or constraints would alter the supply understanding. |

**Traceability:** Business Owner: CA-S-002. Publishes EV-S-010–012 and BN-S-010. Consumes BN-S-001 and BN-D-011. Realises BO-S-001, BO-S-002, BO-S-003, BO-S-005.

*Note:* Consumers marked as stubs (Manage Capacity, Procure Materials, Schedule Production, Manage Distribution, Promise Intelligence, Scenario Intelligence) are planned consumption contracts. Their full specifications will be developed in subsequent versions of the Supply Intelligence specification.
